claims.text: Annealing a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy at approximately 550–600 °C for several hours will increase its coercive field.
The intermediate-temperature anneal will promote a fine dispersion of B2 precipitates within an A2 matrix.
The target alloy initially lacks significant nanoscale phase separation.
The proposed effect applies to a FeCoNi-based composition that permits B2 and A2 phase coexistence.
The anneal will form a fine and stable dispersion of B2 precipitates in the A2 matrix.
B2 precipitates act as magnetic-domain-wall pinning centers.
Restricting magnetic-domain-wall motion through precipitate pinning increases coercivity.
The annealed sample will have a statistically significant coercive-field increase relative to an otherwise identical unannealed sample.
The coercivity enhancement should occur only where thermodynamics and kinetics permit controlled B2/A2 phase decomposition.
Substantially different compositions or prior processing histories may prevent the proposed microstructure or coercivity enhancement.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase and the optimal annealing window may vary with alloy composition and processing history.
A three-hour anneal at 550–600 °C is expected to produce fine B2 precipitates detectable through TEM and XRD.
Observation of B2 precipitates without a statistically significant coercivity increase would falsify the hypothesis.
A coercivity increase without corresponding precipitate formation would falsify the proposed precipitate-mediated hypothesis.
